name: Trimble Connect Model API
description:
# Overview
The Trimble Connect Model Service allows you to execute queries over Building Information Models (BIM).

Documentation for this service is available on the [Trimble Developer](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/model) site.

# Getting started
**You must agree to the [Terms of Service](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/terms) to use Connect services.**

You need to complete the steps in the [Getting started](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/getting_started) guide to be able to call the API.

# Concepts
Please see [Common Concepts](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect#common-concepts) in the Connect Platform overview.

## Files and Models

Models are files in the project that are recognized by the system as 2D or 3D models and have TrimBIM representation attached.
The "modelId" equals to the "fileId" and represent the same identifier in in the context of the Model APIs or File APIs respectively.
Typically models are discovered by selecting a project from a list of projects available to user, then listing files in a project and selecting a file that represents are model.
The Project and File APIs are part of the [Trimble Connect API](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/core-api) surface.

## Model Entity Identifiers
Entities can be referred to by their external (source) Id, as well as by their internal (runtime) Id.

The external (source) Id is assigned to each entity by the authoring application and can take the form of
a GUID, a string or even a number.
The internal (runtime) Id is the numeric index of the entity within the model, ranging from 0 to N-1, where N is the
number of entities in the model.
Some authoring applications do not use external (source) Ids, in which case they will not be available.
Internal (runtime) Ids can always be used.

In cases when external (source) identifier is missing a so called "not persistent" identifier can be generated by the service from the entity geometry.
The "not persistent" identifier is not guaranteed to be constant, but in most cases it is until entity geometry changes.
Such identifiers (external if it exists or generated if external is missing) are referred to as "connect" identifiers.

When passing an entity identifier to an endpoint, it
can be prefixed with `id:` to explicitly specify that it is an external (source)
Id, or with the `idx:` prefix to specify that it is an internal (runtime) Id
(index). The `idc:` prefix can be used to specify that it is a "connect" identifier (meaning that it might be generated if proper source identifier is missing).
Some endpoints also allow passing an index explicitly (which should
always be the internal/runtime Id and needs no prefix). The entity Id prefixes
can be useful to resolve the ambiguity between the two type of entity identifiers
in the case when both the external (source) Ids and internal (runtime) Ids are
numbers. If a prefix is not given, the service will attempt to determine the
type of the Id. If this cannot be done based on the value of the Id (eg. when
it is a number), the service will assume that it's an external (source) Id.

Examples:
* an entity identifier with the value `id:123` will be considered an external (source) Id.
* an entity identifier with the value `idx:123` will be considered an internal (runtime) Id.
* an entity identifier with the value `idc:ABC123` will be considered an "connect" identifier that might be equal to external id or generated from geometry.
* an entity identifier with the value `123` will be primarily considered an "connect" identifier, but if the service
  determines that there are no entities with such "connect" identifiers exist, then it will attempt to use it as an internal (runtime) Id (index).

## Eventual Read Consistency
The service does not perform any write operations and therefore has no database of its own.
The API responses are eventually consistent with the file operations performed with [Trimble Connect
File APIs](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/core-api#tag--Files) and file processing.
When you read data from the service, the response might not reflect the results of the most recently completed write operation in FileService
and file processing. The response might include some stale data due to caching
in place. If you repeat your read request after a short time, the response should return the latest data.

## Paginated Responses
All endpoints that return collection of resources follow the same schema for query parameters and
response structure to paginate the results.
Pagination allows to limit the size of the large responses and aimed to improve the responsiveness and overall
performance when fetching large result sets. The overall latency is improved
by parallelization of data processing and transfer.

Pagination is offset-based and client-driven. The requests accept `offset` and `top` query parameters.
`offset is a non-negative integer, while `top` is a positive integer.`

The `offset` must be less than total number of items in the result set and service
will return an error if offset is out of range to help client catch the error in
the pagination logic.

If the `offset` query parameter is not specified, a default offset=0 is assumed and first page of the result set is returned.
The total size of the result set can be discovered in two ways:
* if request does not contain any filtering on the model data then the total counts for all collections
are available in the GetModelInfo endpoint response.
* if filtering is applied then the total count of the result set will be returned in the first response
as a `total` property

For best performance while fetching a complete result set, it is recommended to fetch the pages in parallel. Client should discover the total
number of items, calculate the number of pages needed and send requests to fetch the pages
in parallel. The level of parallelism should be limited based on the network
bandwidth available to the client, for example max 5 active parallel requests at any moment in time.
The `top` parameter informs the server on how many items client
wants to receive in a single page. Server returns the requested number of items
if they are available or less (for the last page in the result set).
If `top` parameter is not specified then server return maximum page size by default.

The maximum page size is different for each endpoint and specified as part of the endpoint
description. If the `top` parameter is greater than endpoint can support server
will return error to help client avoid bug in pagination implementation.

## Property Data Types, Units and Tolerances

Service supports data types for properties that are closely related to data types supported by `TrimBIM` and [IFC4](http://standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4/FINAL/HTML/) formats.
The list of supported property data types might be expanded in the future.

The measurement data types represent physical measurements and have units.

When comparing numerical values the service supports default non 0 tolerance (ability to compare property values within accepted limits) for some of the property types.
These tolerances will be applied by default when filtering for entities through the simple query API.
The tolerance specified through the request will always override the service level default tolerance.
Absolute tolerance is calculated as AbsTolerance = Abs(expected-actual).

For example: if absolute tolerance defined for mass is 0.001 kg.
  1. If mass is 500 kg (expected) and 501 kg (actual), the calculated absolute difference is 1 kg (> 0.001 kg).
  Since the absolute tolerance is greater than the defined tolerance limits, they are considered different.
  2. If mass is 10 g (expected) and 10.5 g (actual), the calculated absolute difference is 0.5 g (< 0.001 kg).
  Values are considered equal as absolute difference is less than allowed difference.

Below table summarizes the units and tolerances supported for all property data types.


| Property Data Type | Unit                                                           | Default Absolute Tolerance |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| lengthMeasure      | millimeter (mm)                                                |     0.01                   |
| areaMeasure        | square metre (m2)                                              |     0.001                  |
| volumeMeasure      | cubic metre (m3)                                               |     0.0001                 |
| massMeasure        | kilograms (kg)                                                 |     0.001                  |
| angleMeasure       | degree (°)                                                     |     0.000001               |
| integer            |   -                                                            |     0                      |
| number             |   -                                                            |     0.00001                |
| string             |   -                                                            | Case sensitive exact match |
| string:date-time   | [ISO8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)              |     PT0S                   |

Below table summarize mapping of [IFC4](http://standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4/FINAL/HTML/) and TrimBIM property data types to data types used in Model Service.

| TrimBIM Data Type  | IFC4 Data Type        | Model Service Data Type                  | Description                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| LengthMeasure      |  IfcLengthMeasure     | `{"type":"lengthMeasure"}`               |                                                                                                                                     |
| AreaMeasure        |  IfcAreaMeasure       | `{"type":"areaMeasure"}`                 |                                                                                                                                     |
| VolumeMeasure      |  IfcVolumeMeasure     | `{"type":"volumeMeasure"}`               |                                                                                                                                     |
| MassMeasure        |  IfcMassMeasure       | `{"type":"massMeasure"}`                 |                                                                                                                                     |
| AngleMeasure       |  IfcPlaneAngleMeasure | `{"type":"angleMeasure"}`                |                                                                                                                                     |
| IntValue           |  IfcInteger           | `{"type":"integer"}`                     |                                                                                                                                     |
| DoubleValue        |  IfcReal              | `{"type":"number"}`                      |                                                                                                                                     |
| Logical            |  IfcLogical           | `{"type":"boolean", "nullable":true}`    | `false`, `true` or `null`.                                                                                                          |
| Boolean            |  IfcBoolean           | `{"type":"boolean"}`                     | `false`, `true`                                                                                                                     |
| StringValue        |  IfcText              | `{"type":"string"}`                      |                                                                                                                                     |
| DateTime           |  IfcDateTime          | `{"type":"string", "format:"date-time"}` | A string to represent a date and time - [RFC3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339), for example, `2018-11-13T20:20:39+00:00` |

## Limits
The service has the following limits:
* Maximum number of items returned in a single response is specified for each endpoint individually.
